newsitem.title: UK: BA takes contingency plans for strike-paper.
newsitem.headline: BA takes contingency plans for strike-paper.

text.p: British Airways Plc has taken contingency plans in the event of a strike, the Financial Times said on Tuesday.
Cabin crew at the airline on Monday night voted in favour of a series of three-day strikes in a five-month-old dispute over pay and conditions.

The Financial said the company did not deny that employment agency offices over recent months have been recruiting up to one thousand lorry drivers, baggage handlers and loading staff for BA in the Heathrow airport area.
The newspaper quoted BA's chief executive Bob Ayling as saying, "We intend to continue to operate if there are any strikes."
Senior airline managers and other staff have also been trained on to prepare for work as substitute cabin crew, the paper said. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
